title: Q15 — real-tenant authority census for W-20 removal and the OD-7 conversion burndown
status: PREPARED — NOT EXECUTED. No worker-side channel to database.read_census exists in this lane; see access_request.
$comment: A DEDICATED artifact, deliberately not an amendment to wave0-authority-census.json. Promoting amended SQL into that file inherits its stored query_hash and fails query_hash_mismatch — a trap this program has already paid for once. This file carries no query_hash for the same reason: the executing channel should hash what it runs.
read_only_basis: Every statement is a single SELECT. No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ALTER/CREATE/DROP/GRANT, no DO block, no function call that writes. Validated against the local certification database purely to prove the statements parse and return — those results are NOT the census and are not recorded here.
combined_query:
WITH legacy AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id,
         COALESCE(
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(up.role::text)), ''),
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(au1.role::text)), ''),
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(au2.role::text)), '')
         ) AS legacy_role
  FROM auth.users u
  LEFT JOIN public.user_profiles up ON up.id = u.id
  LEFT JOIN public.app_users au1 ON au1.id = u.id
  LEFT JOIN public.app_users au2 ON au2.auth_user_id = u.id
),
a1 AS (
  SELECT l.legacy_role, count(*) AS principals
  FROM legacy l
  WHERE l.legacy_role IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur
      WHERE ur.user_id = l.user_id
        AND NULLIF(lower(btrim(ur.role::text)), '') IS NOT NULL
    )
  GROUP BY l.legacy_role
),
a2 AS (
  SELECT l.legacy_role,
         count(*) AS principals,
         count(*) FILTER (
           WHERE EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur
             WHERE ur.user_id = l.user_id
               AND lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) = l.legacy_role
           )
         ) AS canonical_role_matches,
         count(*) FILTER (
           WHERE NOT EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur
             WHERE ur.user_id = l.user_id
               AND lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) = l.legacy_role
           )
         ) AS canonical_role_differs
  FROM legacy l
  WHERE l.legacy_role IS NOT NULL
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = l.user_id)
  GROUP BY l.legacy_role
),
a3 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.legacy_role,
         EXISTS (
           SELECT 1 FROM public.role_definitions rd WHERE rd.role_key = l.legacy_role
         ) AS is_a_defined_role
  FROM legacy l
  WHERE l.legacy_role IS NOT NULL
),
a4 AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS legacy_only_principals,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE au.org_id IS NULL) AS legacy_row_without_org
  FROM auth.users u
  JOIN public.app_users au ON au.id = u.id OR au.auth_user_id = u.id
  WHERE NULLIF(lower(btrim(au.role::text)), '') IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = u.id)
),
b1 AS (
  SELECT lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) AS role_key,
         count(*) AS memberships,
         count(DISTINCT ur.org_id) AS orgs
  FROM public.user_roles ur
  GROUP BY 1
),
b2 AS (
  SELECT g.role_key,
         g.permission_key,
         count(DISTINCT g.org_id) AS orgs_granting,
         (SELECT count(DISTINCT rd.org_id)
            FROM public.role_definitions rd
           WHERE rd.role_key = g.role_key) AS orgs_defining_role
  FROM public.role_permission_grants g
  WHERE g.allowed
  GROUP BY g.role_key, g.permission_key
),
b3 AS (
  SELECT g.role_key,
         g.permission_key,
         count(DISTINCT g.org_id) AS orgs_granting,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_roles ur
           WHERE lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) = g.role_key) AS memberships_holding_role
  FROM public.role_permission_grants g
  WHERE g.allowed
    AND g.role_key NOT IN ('admin', 'ops')
  GROUP BY g.role_key, g.permission_key
),
b4 AS (
  SELECT rd.role_key,
         pd.key AS permission_key,
         count(*) AS orgs_defining_role_without_grant
  FROM public.role_definitions rd
  CROSS JOIN public.permission_definitions pd
  WHERE rd.role_key IN ('admin', 'ops')
    AND pd.is_active
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.role_permission_grants g
      WHERE g.org_id = rd.org_id
        AND g.role_key = rd.role_key
        AND g.permission_key = pd.key
        AND g.allowed
    )
  GROUP BY rd.role_key, pd.key
  HAVING count(*) > 0
),
c1 AS (
  SELECT g.role_key,
         count(DISTINCT g.org_id) AS orgs_granting,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_roles ur
           WHERE lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) = g.role_key
             AND ur.org_id IN (
               SELECT g2.org_id FROM public.role_permission_grants g2
               WHERE g2.allowed
                 AND g2.permission_key IN ('settings.users_roles.read', 'settings.users_roles')
                 AND g2.role_key = g.role_key
             )) AS memberships_newly_admitted
  FROM public.role_permission_grants g
  WHERE g.allowed
    AND g.permission_key IN ('settings.users_roles.read', 'settings.users_roles')
    AND g.role_key NOT IN ('admin', 'ops')
  GROUP BY g.role_key
),
d1 AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS memberships,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.user_id IS NULL) AS without_access_profile,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.department_scope = 'restricted') AS department_restricted,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.site_scope = 'restricted') AS site_restricted
  FROM public.user_roles ur
  LEFT JOIN public.user_access_profiles p
    ON p.user_id = ur.user_id AND p.org_id = ur.org_id
),
answered AS (
  SELECT 'Q15-A1' AS question_id, (SELECT count(*) FROM a1) AS row_count
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-A2', (SELECT count(*) FROM a2)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-A3', (SELECT count(*) FROM a3)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-A4', (SELECT count(*) FROM a4)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-B1', (SELECT count(*) FROM b1)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-B2', (SELECT count(*) FROM b2)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-B3', (SELECT count(*) FROM b3)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-B4', (SELECT count(*) FROM b4)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-C1', (SELECT count(*) FROM c1)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-D1', (SELECT count(*) FROM d1)
)
SELECT question_id, kind, payload
FROM (
  SELECT ans.question_id, 'row_count' AS kind,
         jsonb_build_object('row_count', ans.row_count) AS payload
  FROM answered ans
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-A1', 'row', to_jsonb(a1) FROM a1
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-A2', 'row', to_jsonb(a2) FROM a2
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-A3', 'row', to_jsonb(a3) FROM a3
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-A4', 'row', to_jsonb(a4) FROM a4
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-B1', 'row', to_jsonb(b1) FROM b1
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-B2', 'row', to_jsonb(b2) FROM b2
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-B3', 'row', to_jsonb(b3) FROM b3
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-B4', 'row', to_jsonb(b4) FROM b4
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-C1', 'row', to_jsonb(c1) FROM c1
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q15-D1', 'row', to_jsonb(d1) FROM d1
) census
ORDER BY question_id, kind, payload::text;
combined_query_basis: The trusted-host action reads ONE field from a JSON artifact — trusted-host-action-registry.mjs takes j.combined_query || j.sql || j.query and rejects the artifact with json_missing_sql if none is present, then requires a SINGLE statement beginning WITH or SELECT. The nine per-question statements below are the readable form and remain the authority for what each question means; this field is their executable projection and must stay semantically identical to them. Proven, not asserted: validateReadOnlySql returns {ok:true,kind:'with_select'}, and the statement was executed against a real PostgreSQL to prove it parses and returns. Those cert-tenant numbers are NOT the census and are recorded nowhere.
combined_query_shape: Rows are (question_id, kind, payload). Every question emits exactly one kind='row_count' row even when it matches nothing, so 'this question returned zero' is distinguishable from 'this question never ran' — the decision rules below turn on zero/non-zero, and a silently skipped query would read as a clean result. kind='row' rows carry that question's own columns as jsonb.
combined_query_hash_absent_deliberately: No hash is stored, for the reason in $comment: the validator compares a stored query_hash against what it is about to run and fails query_hash_mismatch on any drift. The executing channel should hash what it runs.

data_minimization.returns: role keys, capability keys, aggregate counts, boolean coverage, mismatch categories
data_minimization.never_returns: names, emails, phone numbers, child or family data, communications, operational records
data_minimization.identifier_policy: No query selects a name or address column. A1 and C1 return counts only; if an anomaly needs a specific principal, re-run that one query with a user_id projection as a follow-up rather than widening these.

resolver_facts_the_sql_mirrors.legacy_is_a_FALLBACK_not_a_parallel_path: resolveAdminAccessCore consults user_profiles/app_users ONLY when chooseOrgAndRoleKeysFromMembershipRows returns null — i.e. when the principal has no usable user_roles row. So the lockout population is exactly: legacy role present AND no usable canonical membership. A principal with both is unaffected by removal, because the fallback is never reached for them.
resolver_facts_the_sql_mirrors.three_legacy_reads: user_profiles.role by id; app_users.role/org_id by id; app_users.role/org_id by auth_user_id. The third exists because the two tables key differently, and a census that checked only the first two would under-count.
resolver_facts_the_sql_mirrors.normalization: normalizeRoleKey trims and lowercases, so the SQL uses lower(btrim(role)) rather than raw equality — a row holding 'Admin ' authorizes today and a raw comparison would miss it.
resolver_facts_the_sql_mirrors.portal_roles: portalEligible is roleKeys ∩ {admin, ops}. requireAdminOrOps admits on that set by ROLE, never by grant, which is why B3/B4 are the load-bearing queries for OD-7.
resolver_facts_the_sql_mirrors.role_column_types: user_profiles.role is the ENUM app_role, not text, so btrim() rejects it without a cast — caught by validating these statements against a real PostgreSQL rather than by reading them. Every role column is cast ::text before normalization; casting text to text is a no-op, so the same SQL is correct whichever type a given deployment carries.

questions.question: How many principals would LOSE all authority if the two legacy reads were removed? (legacy role present, no usable canonical membership)
questions.decides: W-20 removal is safe only if this is 0.
questions.sql:
WITH legacy AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id,
         COALESCE(
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(up.role::text)), ''),
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(au1.role::text)), ''),
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(au2.role::text)), '')
         ) AS legacy_role
  FROM auth.users u
  LEFT JOIN public.user_profiles up ON up.id = u.id
  LEFT JOIN public.app_users au1 ON au1.id = u.id
  LEFT JOIN public.app_users au2 ON au2.auth_user_id = u.id
)
SELECT l.legacy_role,
       count(*) AS principals
FROM legacy l
WHERE l.legacy_role IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur
    WHERE ur.user_id = l.user_id
      AND NULLIF(lower(btrim(ur.role::text)), '') IS NOT NULL
  )
GROUP BY l.legacy_role
ORDER BY principals DESC;

questions.question: How many legacy values are REDUNDANT — a canonical membership exists, so the fallback is never consulted?
questions.sql:
WITH legacy AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id,
         COALESCE(
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(up.role::text)), ''),
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(au1.role::text)), ''),
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(au2.role::text)), '')
         ) AS legacy_role
  FROM auth.users u
  LEFT JOIN public.user_profiles up ON up.id = u.id
  LEFT JOIN public.app_users au1 ON au1.id = u.id
  LEFT JOIN public.app_users au2 ON au2.auth_user_id = u.id
)
SELECT l.legacy_role,
       count(*) AS principals,
       count(*) FILTER (
         WHERE EXISTS (
           SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur
           WHERE ur.user_id = l.user_id
             AND lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) = l.legacy_role
         )
       ) AS canonical_role_matches,
       count(*) FILTER (
         WHERE NOT EXISTS (
           SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur
           WHERE ur.user_id = l.user_id
             AND lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) = l.legacy_role
         )
       ) AS canonical_role_differs
FROM legacy l
WHERE l.legacy_role IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = l.user_id)
GROUP BY l.legacy_role
ORDER BY principals DESC;

questions.question: How many legacy values are STALE — naming a role no org actually defines?
questions.note: A legacy role that is not a role_definitions key anywhere cannot become a capability holder, so removing it cannot narrow anything. This also re-tests W-44's premise against real data rather than seed data.
questions.sql:
WITH legacy AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(up.role::text)), ''),
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(au1.role::text)), ''),
           NULLIF(lower(btrim(au2.role::text)), '')
         ) AS legacy_role
  FROM auth.users u
  LEFT JOIN public.user_profiles up ON up.id = u.id
  LEFT JOIN public.app_users au1 ON au1.id = u.id
  LEFT JOIN public.app_users au2 ON au2.auth_user_id = u.id
)
SELECT l.legacy_role,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.role_definitions rd WHERE rd.role_key = l.legacy_role) AS is_a_defined_role
FROM legacy l
WHERE l.legacy_role IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY is_a_defined_role, l.legacy_role;

questions.question: For principals reachable only through the fallback, does the legacy org agree with any canonical org they hold?
questions.sql:
SELECT count(*) AS legacy_only_principals,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE au.org_id IS NULL) AS legacy_row_without_org
FROM auth.users u
JOIN public.app_users au ON au.id = u.id OR au.auth_user_id = u.id
WHERE NULLIF(lower(btrim(au.role::text)), '') IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = u.id);

questions.question: Which role keys exist, and how many memberships does each carry?
questions.sql:
SELECT lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) AS role_key,
       count(*) AS memberships,
       count(DISTINCT ur.org_id) AS orgs
FROM public.user_roles ur
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY memberships DESC;

questions.question: Role × capability coverage — which canonical capabilities does each role actually receive?
questions.sql:
SELECT g.role_key,
       g.permission_key,
       count(DISTINCT g.org_id) AS orgs_granting,
       (SELECT count(DISTINCT rd.org_id) FROM public.role_definitions rd WHERE rd.role_key = g.role_key) AS orgs_defining_role
FROM public.role_permission_grants g
WHERE g.allowed
GROUP BY g.role_key, g.permission_key
ORDER BY g.role_key, g.permission_key;

questions.question: WIDENING evidence — which NON admin/ops roles hold capabilities, and how many principals do they represent?
questions.decides: A pure capability conversion of a requireAdminOrOps gate admits exactly these principals in addition to today's. If this is empty, conversion is equal-admission; if not, it is wider and OD-7 rule 6 makes it an exception.
questions.sql:
SELECT g.role_key,
       g.permission_key,
       count(DISTINCT g.org_id) AS orgs_granting,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_roles ur
         WHERE lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) = g.role_key) AS memberships_holding_role
FROM public.role_permission_grants g
WHERE g.allowed
  AND g.role_key NOT IN ('admin', 'ops')
GROUP BY g.role_key, g.permission_key
ORDER BY memberships_holding_role DESC, g.role_key, g.permission_key;

questions.question: NARROWING evidence — for each capability, which orgs define admin/ops WITHOUT granting it?
questions.decides: A capability conversion narrows for exactly these org/role pairs: the role is admitted by requireAdminOrOps today and would not hold the capability tomorrow. Non-zero means the conversion needs a preservation grant or is not the right target.
questions.sql:
SELECT rd.role_key,
       pd.key AS permission_key,
       count(*) AS orgs_defining_role_without_grant
FROM public.role_definitions rd
CROSS JOIN public.permission_definitions pd
WHERE rd.role_key IN ('admin', 'ops')
  AND pd.is_active
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.role_permission_grants g
    WHERE g.org_id = rd.org_id
      AND g.role_key = rd.role_key
      AND g.permission_key = pd.key
      AND g.allowed
  )
GROUP BY rd.role_key, pd.key
HAVING count(*) > 0
ORDER BY orgs_defining_role_without_grant DESC, rd.role_key, pd.key;

questions.question: admin/users EXCEPTION — do real principals hold settings.users_roles.read through a role that is NOT admin/ops?
questions.decides: These are exactly the principals who would GAIN roster read if admin/users GET converted from portal admission to settings.users_roles.read. Non-zero confirms the recorded widening is real rather than theoretical. Evidence only — the product decision is not this census's to make.
questions.sql:
SELECT g.role_key,
       count(DISTINCT g.org_id) AS orgs_granting,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_roles ur
         WHERE lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) = g.role_key
           AND ur.org_id = ANY (array_agg(DISTINCT g.org_id))) AS memberships_newly_admitted
FROM public.role_permission_grants g
WHERE g.allowed
  AND g.permission_key IN ('settings.users_roles.read', 'settings.users_roles')
  AND g.role_key NOT IN ('admin', 'ops')
GROUP BY g.role_key
ORDER BY orgs_granting DESC;

questions.question: Does scope remain independently enforced — how many memberships carry an access profile, and how many are restricted?
questions.note: Capability possession is not scope. This confirms the Scope layer is populated independently of Role, so a capability conversion cannot be read as granting org-wide reach.
questions.sql:
SELECT count(*) AS memberships,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.user_id IS NULL) AS without_access_profile,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.department_scope = 'restricted') AS department_restricted,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.site_scope = 'restricted') AS site_restricted
FROM public.user_roles ur
LEFT JOIN public.user_access_profiles p
  ON p.user_id = ur.user_id AND p.org_id = ur.org_id;

decision_rules.W-20_removal_safe_iff: Q15-A1 returns zero principals. A non-zero result is a lockout population and W-20's removal half stays blocked regardless of how tidy the code would become.
decision_rules.OD-7_conversion_equal_iff: Q15-B3 is empty for the capability in question (nobody outside admin/ops holds it) AND Q15-B4 is zero for that capability (no admin/ops org lacks it). Either alone is insufficient: B3 alone permits a silent narrowing, B4 alone permits a silent widening.
decision_rules.admin_users_exception_resolved_iff: Q15-C1 returns zero. Non-zero keeps it a named exception and the reconciliation needs a product decision, not more evidence.

access_request.why_not_executed: No worker-side channel to database.read_census exists in this lane. Established by inspection, not assumption: this worktree holds only web/.env.certification.local pointing at 127.0.0.1:54421; alloy-ro declares network=false and credential_access=false; vac brokers only typecheck/test/build/playwright/imports; the Vacilando control plane on 127.0.0.1:3020 is live but every endpoint returns 401 with auth_required=true, and no VACILANDO_* token is present in this lane's environment or filesystem.
access_request.minimal_ask: Execute the questions in this file via the trusted-host database.read_census action against alloy_deployed_primary, and return the result rows.
access_request.sufficient_alternative: A read-only connection string for a role with SELECT on public.user_roles, public.role_definitions, public.role_permission_grants, public.permission_definitions, public.user_access_profiles, public.user_profiles, public.app_users and auth.users. Nothing here writes, and nothing selects a name, address or contact column.
access_request.explicitly_refused_substitute: The certification tenant. It defines only admin and ops with no custom roles, so it would report Q15-B3 and Q15-C1 as empty and Q15-A1 as zero — reading exactly like a clean bill of health while proving nothing about deployed authority. Substituting it would manufacture the answer the census exists to test.
